title: Rosalind and the Alibi
premise: Juniper Iversen, the quiet archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, discovers that the diary of Edith Marlowe—a woman who vanished three years ago—contains entries written after her disappearance, hidden in the crypt's locked archive. As Juniper investigates, she realizes someone with intimate knowledge of the case files has been staging evidence to frame a dead man, and that her own predecessor's 'retirement' was anything but voluntary. With the anniversary dinner approaching and the killer closing in, Juniper must use her mastery of the archives to set a trap. In the end, she exposes the cathedral's beloved verger as Edith's killer, inherits both Edith's diary and her unfinished mission of protecting the town's forgotten people, and finally claims a place in the community she'd always observed from behind the filing cabinets.
about_author: Gideon Hartwell is a former parish records clerk from the English coast who spent a decade cataloguing other people's secrets before turning to fiction. His novels explore the quiet violence hidden inside small communities and the strangers who learn to call them home.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Absence
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Establishing chapter: Juniper catalogs the cathedral archive on the eve of Edith Marlowe's third-anniversary memorial, revealing her self-imposed invisibility and her careful distance from townsfolk who barely know her name. She finds an uncatalogued box marked with Edith's name that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as order.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Reading Edith's diary by lamplight, Juniper discovers entries continuing eight months past the disappearance date—written in Edith's hand, describing places only Edith knew. The final entry names 'the keeper of keys.' Detective Inspector Sorrel dismisses her theory; the case is closed. Emotional beat: dread mixed with exhilaration—someone is alive, or something is very wrong.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Juniper breaks into the locked crypt and finds Edith's coat, a second diary half-burned, and fresh footprints in centuries-old dust—someone visits regularly. She notices the crypt key log has been altered, entries removed with archival precision: her own professional technique. Emotional beat: violation; her safe world of paper has been weaponized.

chapters.title: The Verger's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Warm interlude: verger Tobias Fenwick brings her tea, shares memories of Edith, and offers Juniper the belonging she's starved for—the first person to truly see her. But he mentions a detail about the key log that contradicts his earlier account. Emotional beat: found family blooming alongside first seeds of doubt.

chapters.title: A Predecessor's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Tracking down her predecessor Margaret Hale, now living far away, Juniper learns Margaret discovered anomalies in the archive before her abrupt departure—and warns Juniper: 'Whoever it is doesn't hide things. They file them.' Margaret fled after a threat delivered through a perfectly shelved book. Emotional beat: fear becoming personal.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: POV alternating Juniper/Sorrel. The town prepares the memorial dinner while Sorrel quietly reopens the case after Juniper shows him the post-disappearance entries. Someone ransacks Juniper's office but takes nothing—except one page of the diary, leaving a replacement forged so well only she could spot it. Emotional beat: the hunter realizes she is hunted.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Deciphering the burned diary's fragments, Juniper reconstructs Edith's secret: she'd been secretly documenting the town's hidden histories—illegitimate children, stolen inheritances—including a bequest the cathedral quietly absorbed decades ago. The inheritance theme crystallizes: Edith died because she meant to give it back. Emotional beat: righteous anger on behalf of the erased.

chapters.title: Filed Under M for Marlowe
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Following the filing logic of the altered records, Juniper deduces the killer's identity pattern and sets a trap: she plants a false diary page suggesting the original bequest documents survive in the crypt, then waits through the night among the shelves. Footsteps come. She sees the lantern light—and recognizes the hands holding it. Emotional beat: cold clarity; heartbreak and resolve fused.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Keys
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Climax in the crypt during the anniversary dinner above: Tobias Fenwick confesses—he killed Edith to protect the cathedral's stolen inheritance and has been curating the evidence ever since, believing himself its faithful archivist. He traps Juniper among the tombs; she escapes using her knowledge of the crypt's false catacomb passage—a detail only a true archivist would know. Sorrel arrives as the dinner toast echoes overhead. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Resolution: Edith's remains are laid to rest, the bequest restored to its rightful heirs, and Juniper is formally appointed keeper of the full archive—with Edith's diary entrusted to her care. At last invited to sit at the community table rather than catalog it, she writes the first entry of her own record. Emotional beat: grief settled into belonging; invisibility voluntarily ended.
